# StatusDot

A status dot that shows a status with a semantic color. The accessible name comes from `aria-label`, or the
default name of the tone when omitted; combine it with Text when visible text is needed.

**Category**: Basic · **Common uses**: Online status, status of a service or connection, the status badge at the corner of an avatar

## Import

```ts
import { StatusDot } from 'vellum-ui'
```

## Basic usage

The caller maps the business meaning to a tone and describes it with `aria-label`; combine it with Text when
visible text is shown next to it.

```tsx
import { Inline, StatusDot, Text } from 'vellum-ui'

export function Basic() {
  return (
    <Inline gap={4}>
      <Inline gap={1}>
        <StatusDot tone="success" aria-label="Online" />
        <Text size="sm">Online</Text>
      </Inline>
      <Inline gap={1}>
        <StatusDot tone="warning" aria-label="Away" />
        <Text size="sm">Away</Text>
      </Inline>
      <Inline gap={1}>
        <StatusDot tone="neutral" aria-label="Offline" />
        <Text size="sm">Offline</Text>
      </Inline>
    </Inline>
  )
}
```

## Variants

### All tones

`success` normal, `warning` attention, `danger` error, `neutral` inactive, `accent` notice.

```tsx
import { Inline, StatusDot } from 'vellum-ui'

export function Tones() {
  return (
    <Inline gap={3}>
      <StatusDot tone="success" aria-label="Running" />
      <StatusDot tone="warning" aria-label="Sync delayed" />
      <StatusDot tone="danger" aria-label="Connection failed" />
      <StatusDot tone="neutral" aria-label="Disabled" />
      <StatusDot tone="accent" aria-label="Update available" />
    </Inline>
  )
}
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tone` | `'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger' \| 'neutral' \| 'accent'` | Tone: `success` for normal, `warning` for attention, `danger` for errors, `neutral` for inactive, `accent` for reminders. The caller maps business meanings (online, running, disabled, and so on) to tones and describes them with `aria-label`. | — | Yes |

Also accepts `testId` (rendered as `data-testid`), `aria-label`, `role` and `id`, like all primitives.

Does not accept `style` or `className`: appearance is adjusted only through the semantic props above and the theme.
